anomalies.obs: Both MCP2515 CAN controllers are wired to the same SPI chip‑select and MISO nets: U44 pin16 (CS)=NET0170 and pin15 (S0)=NET0065, and U40 pin16 (CS)=NET0170 and pin15 (S0)=NET0065. The two controllers therefore share one CS line and have their SO/MISO outputs tied together.
anomalies.expected: The spec states 'two isolated CAN buses (CAN0, CAN1), each driven by its own MCP2515 SPI CAN controller (U8, U9)'. Two SPI slaves on a shared bus must have independent chip‑selects and must not have their MISO outputs paralleled.

evidence.quote: CAN BUS page: U44 MCP2515‑xSO pins 14/15/16/13 = NET0211/NET0065/NET0170/NET0205; U40 MCP2515‑xSO pins 14/15/16/13 = NET0211/NET0065/NET0170/NET0205 (identical)
two isolated CAN buses (CAN0, CAN1), each driven by its own MCP2515 SPI CAN controller (U8, U9)

anomalies.impact: Both CAN controllers are selected simultaneously and their MISO drivers fight, causing SPI bus contention; the two CAN buses cannot be addressed independently and at least one (likely both) will not communicate.

anomalies.obs: The two M12 CAN connectors carry the same set of differential‑pair nets: J35 (CAN Interface A) pins 2/3/5/8 = NET0064/NET0187/NET0002/NET0153 and J36 (CAN Interface B) pins 2/3/5/8 = NET0064/NET0187/NET0002/NET0153. U4's bus is NET0002/NET0187 and U12's bus is NET0064/NET0153, so each connector mixes one line from each bus on its adjacent pins, and the termination network (SW10 with R33/R90) pairs NET0153↔NET0187 and NET0002↔NET0064, i.e. cross‑bus.
anomalies.expected: Per the spec, CAN0 and CAN1 are separate isolated buses, each broken out on its own connector ('CAN Interface A' = CAN0, 'CAN Interface B' = CAN1); a 120R termination must sit across each bus's own CANH/CANL pair.

evidence.quote: CAN BUS page: J35 'CAN Interface A' and J36 'CAN Interface B' both show pins 2,3,5,8 = NET0064, NET0187, NET0002, NET0153; U4 CANH/CANL = NET0002/NET0187, U12 CANH/CANL = NET0064/NET0153; SW10+R33/R90 tie NET0153‑NET0187 and NET0002‑NET0064
two isolated CAN buses (CAN0, CAN1) ... broken out on M12 circular connectors J2 ('CAN Interface A') and J13 ('CAN Interface B')

anomalies.impact: A standard two‑wire CAN cable plugged into either connector joins one line of CAN0 to one line of CAN1, shorting/mis‑pairing the two isolated buses; both buses fail or interfere and galvanic isolation is lost.

parsed.summary: The CAN subsystem appears mis‑wired in this build: the two MCP2515 controllers share the same SPI CS and MISO nets, and the two M12 CAN connectors carry the same (cross‑paired) set of CAN0/CAN1 differential nets, so the two buses the spec describes as separate and isolated are effectively merged/shorted at both the controller SPI side and the connector side.
